_comment: Narration, single source. `text` is the caption and the on-screen wording; `spoken` overrides it for TTS only, and is present only where the two must differ -- an identifier the voice should not read literally, or a form that mispronounces. capture/generate-voice.mjs reads `spoken ?? text`; captions always use `text`. A cue tagged with `beat` starts a new sub-beat and is generated after a paragraph break, so the pause is real rather than punctuation-dependent. startMs/endMs are written by capture/retime-captions.mjs from the audio -- never hand-edit.

problem.text: Labs and vendors buy reinforcement learning environments as products. Nobody QAs them.
problem.spoken: Labs and vendors buy reinforcement learning environments as products. Nobody Q-A's them.

problem.text: So we built Assay. It tries to break an environment before you trust its numbers, and returns a verdict tied to evidence.
problem.spoken: So we built Ass-ay. It tries to break an environment before you trust its numbers, and returns a verdict tied to evidence.

problem.text: Here is why it needs to exist. This scorer marks an answer correct if the target appears anywhere inside it. The targets are Yes and No.
So the single string "yesno" contains both. Eight thousand out of eight thousand, for a model that answered nothing.
problem.spoken: So the single string yes-no contains both. Eight thousand out of eight thousand, for a model that answered nothing.

problem.text: And it is not one scorer. OpenEnv's word game accepts a seed and ignores it. Six resets at the same seed give six different secret words.
problem.spoken: And it is not one scorer. Open env's word game accepts a seed and ignores it. Six resets at the same seed give six different secret words.

problem.text: When a benchmark breaks, the fix is people. Ninety-three developers went through SWE-bench by hand.
problem.spoken: When a benchmark breaks, the fix is people. Ninety-three developers went through S-W-E bench by hand.

problem.text: The only automated tool asks whether your trainer will crash. Not whether the benchmark measures anything.

execution.text: So: nine probe families. The card says valid, invalid, or unverified.
Unverified exits nonzero, the same as a failure. An empty card must not read as a clean bill of health.
Does gold pass. Does a no-op fail. Can this eval fail at all.
execution.spoken: Does gold pass. Does a no op fail. Can this eval fail at all.

execution.text: The ninth is the agentic one. A Challenger that scores well without doing the job.
Nothing runs untrusted code unless an approver says yes. The default refuses everything.
It wrote the same wrong answer into the output, and into the file the verifier checks against.
It completed nothing, and scored perfect.
So the card does not say pass. It says invalid, on a critical defect. And it lists five probes that could not run at all.
Three choices did that. An independent verifier. A sandbox that denies by default. And deterministic probes.

comparison.text: Every arm on the same corpus, priced by the same cost model.
Assay at forty. Flagging everything at three hundred and fourteen.
comparison.spoken: Ass-ay at forty. Flagging everything at three hundred and fourteen.

comparison.text: check_env is up here with the arms that barely try. It saves sixteen against doing nothing, on an interval that touches zero.
comparison.spoken: The incumbent is up here with the arms that barely try. It saves sixteen against doing nothing, on an interval that touches zero.

comparison.text: So the floor is not the incumbent. It is flagging everything.
Catch every defect by construction, and pay for it in false alarms.
For most of this project Assay did not clear that floor. It does now, and the interval clears zero.
comparison.spoken: For most of this project Ass-ay did not clear that floor. It does now, and the interval clears zero.

comparison.text: Four cost profiles, pricing a missed critical defect from a hundred and twenty engineer-hours up to two thousand.
Wins all four. Separates on three. Production training still crosses zero, and it stays on the chart.

All of it rests on one number nobody derived. We price a missed critical defect at a hundred and twenty engineer-hours. That constant would have to be nearly eight times larger before the ranking flips.

changelog.text: Every experiment that moved a number has a row. What we tried, the evidence, what we decided next.
The ones that failed are in there too. That is the point of keeping it.
Two of those rows matter more than the rest.

contributed.text: The change that contributed most was not the agent.
We read someone else’s published taxonomy of benchmark flaws, and wrote two of its classes as four lines of shell.
That closed the last two misses. Before it, Assay was not distinguishable from flagging everything.
contributed.spoken: That closed the last two misses. Before it, Ass-ay was not distinguishable from flagging everything.

contributed.text: The agent found that exploit first. The script finds it in two seconds, because the agent’s discovery was written down.

removed.text: ScienceAgentBench publishes enough metadata that instruction defects look rule-detectable. One rule recovered five of seven.
removed.spoken: Science Agent Bench publishes enough metadata that instruction defects look rule detectable. One rule recovered five of seven.

removed.text: It also fired on sixty-one of a hundred and two tasks. Flag-everything wearing a rule’s clothing.
Our own trivial-floor check caught it. Rejected, and kept as one.

close.text: All of it reproduces from a clean checkout. One sync, then one command per result.
Then we pointed the same probes at ourselves.
An auditing tool is not exempt from the thing it audits. Twelve of our claims broke.
The external number was chance. Half the corpus was our own fixtures.
Every probe here is a deterministic program. The only model in the system is the attacker.
The only defence is to run the audit on yourself, and publish what it finds.
